title: What this simulation assumes
intro: These numbers are made up to teach an idea. They are not forecasts. Change them and see how the answer moves.
rates.title: Growth, ups and downs, and fees
rates.row: Grows about {mean} a year, swings about {vol}, fee {fee} a year
inflation.title: Inflation
inflation.row: Prices rise {rate} a year in this simulation.
ignores.title: What this leaves out
ignores.surprises: Surprises the real world can bring, such as a company failing or a new rule.
ignores.behaviour: How you might act when the price falls, such as selling in a panic.
range: Between {low} and {high} in most simulated futures
range.confidence: Most means 90 out of 100 simulated futures
chart.title: 500 simulated futures
chart.alt: After {years} years you put in {invested}. In most simulated futures you end between {low} and {high}. The middle outcome is {median}.
real.hint: Prices go up over time, so a rupee later buys less than a rupee today. Switch on the inflation adjustment to see what that does.
real.title: Why did the chart change?
real.why: Prices rise {rate} a year. So ₹1 in year {years} buys only what {worth} buys today. With the switch on, every amount is shown in today's money. That is why the lines sit lower, and the gap grows the further right you look.
real.end: At the end, the middle outcome is {nominal} in plain rupees, but only about {real} in today's money.
real.dashed: The dashed line drops too, because money you add later is also worth less than money you add now.
real.slow: If a path grows slower than prices rise, its line can fall even while the plain amount goes up. That is how savings lose buying power.
real.learn: Learn more in the Inflation room
